notes.purpose: Shows one unit's sensor readings with a short history and lets the worker see and set the ventilation fan.

elements.name: Sensors control
elements.shows: Sensors · Last reading 09:40 · Temperature 22.4 °C · Humidity 64 % · Ammonia 8 ppm NH₃

states.when: The unit has a finite numeric reading for it
states.shows: A segment with the sensor name over its value and unit (°C, %, ppm NH₃); the first is selected on entry. All present sensors show their value at once.

states.when: Reading missing or not a finite number
states.shows: The segment is omitted, never shown as 0

states.when: None of the three has a value
states.shows: No sensors section, chart or history; only the fan, if any

elements.logic: Sample figures per unit (Unit 7: 22.4 °C, 64 %, 8 ppm). "Last reading" is unitContext[N].updated, one fixed sample time for every sensor.

elements.name: Trend chart
elements.shows: Today · 7 days · a line with its High and Low marked where they happen

states.shows: 8 points from 00:00 to the last reading time
7 daily points (6d ago … Today)

elements.logic: Not real history: series = current value plus fixed offsets scaled by sensor (temperature ×1, humidity ×6, ammonia ×2). Low and High are the min and max of the plotted points; the last point (filled) is the last reading. There is no y axis. The chart is hand-drawn SVG; no design-system chart exists yet (proposed as "Trend chart").

elements.name: View history
elements.shows: A link in the Trend heading that opens a sheet listing the plotted points (time, value and unit)
elements.rule: The sheet lists exactly the plotted points for the selected sensor and period; Back returns to the page.

elements.name: Offline notice
elements.shows: Offline · Showing the last readings. Reconnect to change device settings.

states.when: Page default (the "Connection preview" select outside the phone)
states.shows: The notice at the top, once. The fan shows its state only: Auto/Manual and Save are left out, not greyed.
No notice; the fan shows Auto/Manual, and Save once the draft differs from the applied setting

elements.name: Ventilation fan row
elements.shows: Devices · Ventilation fan · Auto · following unit schedule ›

states.shows: "Auto · following unit schedule"
"Manual · N% speed" (initial speed 45)
The row is read-only: no ›, no tap. The notice at the top says why.

states.when: The unit has no controllable device (devices lacks "fan")
states.shows: The Devices section is absent; only sensors show

elements.logic: Controllable devices are independent of readings: a unit can have devices with no readings (the unit card then says "N devices") or readings with no device.
elements.rule: Tapping the row (connected only) opens the fan sheet. The setting lives in memory only; nothing is sent to equipment.

copy: (raw) every string is literal in home-astra-prototype.js; the registry has no environment ids
edge: A unit with neither readings nor devices has no environment entrance on its Home screen.
issues: The "Last reading" time is a fixed 09:40 on all sensors while the status bar reads 9:41.
Only a ventilation fan exists; the concept names "devices" in general.
The PRD says the fan is disabled offline; the screen makes the fan row read-only instead and shows no controls (the design system prefers omission). Filed for the owner.
unclear: alert thresholds, who is told when a reading is out of range, and where real data comes from; none are in the code.

notes.purpose: Lets the worker set a fixed fan speed instead of the unit schedule.

elements.name: Fan sheet
elements.shows: Ventilation fan · Auto | Manual · Fan speed (%) 45 · Unsaved · Back | Save setting

states.when: Manual pressed, speed stepped, not applied
states.shows: A stepper with − and + (5 % a tap, 0-100) and the number large; "Unsaved" under it; Save setting appears beside Back
The sheet closes; the fan row reads "Manual · 70% speed"; toast "Sample setting saved · no equipment command sent"
The stepper goes away; Save leaves when the draft equals the applied setting

elements.rule: The draft is not applied until Save. Back leaves and keeps the draft: reopening the sheet shows it. The sheet only opens when connected. Preview only: no command is sent to equipment.
elements.source: fan-edit, fan-mode, fan-speed and apply-device handlers

issues: No confirmation or safety limit for speed 0; unclear whether 0% is allowed on a real fan.
Moving a long way takes many taps (5 % each); a slider was dropped because it is hard to set with gloves.

screens.name: Maintenance · open issue
screens.zh: 维修 · 有未解决问题

notes.purpose: Lists the unit's equipment issues and lets the worker report one.

elements.name: Issue card
elements.shows: Drinking station · Open · Pen C2 · Leaking valve at the east end. · G. Hansen · 06:40

states.shows: Equipment name, "Open", location, note, reporter and time
Dimmed with "Resolved"; stays in the list
Reporter reads "G. Hansen · just now", at the top of the list

elements.logic: Location and note are free text typed by the reporter.
elements.at: Leaking valve at the east end.

elements.name: Open count
elements.logic: Records not resolved, singular or plural. The same count feeds the Maintenance chip on the unit screen. Unit 7 starts with one open issue; the `attention` param hides it (clear, health, feed) or adds a default one in other units (maintenance, busy).
elements.rule: Only reachable once a unit is chosen: the Toolbox row exists only in a unit scope. Issues are unit-scoped.

edge: Resolved issues stay listed, so the list is not empty after the only issue is resolved.
issues: The path here is Toolbox, two taps from the unit; the unit screen's Maintenance chip does not link here.
No photo, priority, assignee, or history of who resolved it.

notes.purpose: The empty state when the unit has no issue.

states.when: The unit has no records at all (Unit 8)
states.shows: "No open issues — Report equipment that needs attention in this unit." and "0 open issues"
Not this state: the resolved cards stay listed with "0 open issues"

notes.purpose: Captures a new equipment issue in three fields.

elements.name: Form and Save
elements.shows: Equipment · Location in Unit 7 · What needs attention? · Save sample issue
elements.logic: Equipment (max 80) and Location (max 80, label names the unit) are free text; Note is a textarea (max 500). Save adds an open record at the top with reporter "G. Hansen · just now", closes the drawer and toasts "Issue saved in this preview".
elements.rule: All three fields are required; whitespace-only values are ignored.

issues: Equipment and location are free text; no list of the unit's devices or pens is offered.

notes.purpose: Shows one issue and lets the worker mark it resolved.

elements.name: Mark resolved
elements.logic: Sets resolved on the record, closes the drawer and toasts "Issue resolved in this preview"; the open count drops.
elements.rule: No note is asked and no resolver or time is recorded.

issues: Resolving needs no note and records no resolver or time.

elements.name: Resolved line
elements.shows: Pen C2 · Resolved · Resolved in this preview.

states.shows: The Mark resolved button is replaced by a static line; no action is offered

elements.rule: A resolved issue cannot be reopened.

notes.purpose: The same sensor page switched from today to the last seven days.

elements.name: Chart and history
elements.shows: Seven daily points (6d ago to Today) with High and Low marked; View history lists the same points
elements.logic: The week series is sample data derived from the current reading; the Today series has eight points up to the last-reading time. Low and High are the minimum and maximum of the plotted points.

issues: The chart switch does not change "Last reading" (still 09:40).

notes.purpose: The sensor page with another sensor selected.

elements.name: Sensor switch
elements.shows: Segment of the sensors the unit has, each with its current value: Temperature, Humidity, Ammonia

states.shows: That sensor is omitted from the switch, never shown as 0

states.when: Only one sensor has a reading
states.shows: The switch lists only it; the page opens on it

elements.logic: Unit and chart scale differ per sensor (°C, %, ppm NH₃). The chart is scaled to the plotted points of the selected sensor.
